name: Tyla
description:
'''Tyla Laura Seethal''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|t|aɪ|l|ə}} {{respell|TY|luh}}; born 30 January 2002) is a South African singer and songwriter. Dubbed as the "[[Honorific nicknames in popular music|Queen of Popiano]]", her musical style is characterised by a fusion of [[Pop music|pop]] and [[amapiano]]. Tyla gained international recognition after the release of 2023's "[[Water (Tyla song)|Water]]", which entered the top ten in multiple countries including her native South Africa, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

Born and raised in the [[East Rand]] of [[Johannesburg]], Tyla signed with [[Epic Records]] in 2021 following the domestic success of her 2019 debut single, "[[Getting Late (Tyla song)|Getting Late]]". Her single "Water" was the first song by a South African soloist to enter the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] in 55 years and was awarded the inaugural [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Award]] for [[Grammy Award for Best African Music Performance|Best African Music Performance]]. The single preceded her [[Tyla (album)|self-titled debut album]] (2024), which was released to critical acclaim and moderate commercial success. In 2025, she released the [[extended play]] (EP) ''[[WWP (EP)|WWP]]'', and embarked on its [[We Wanna Party Tour|accompanying tour]]. This was followed by her second studio album, ''[[A*Pop]]'' (2026), which received critical praise and spawned the [[Billboard Global 200|''Billboard'' Global 200]] top-twenty single "[[Chanel (Tyla song)|Chanel]]".

Tyla is the youngest African artist in history to win a [[Grammy Award]], with two wins. Her other [[List of awards and nominations received by Tyla|accolades]] include two [[MTV Video Music Awards]], two [[BET Awards]], three [[MTV Europe Music Awards]], among nominations for a [[Brit Awards|BRIT Award]], an [[Ivor Novello Awards|Ivor Novello Award]], a [[Soul Train Music Awards|Soul Train Music Award]] and nine [[South African Music Awards]].
